dedupe_keys.name: geospatial residential electricity demand under socioeconomic inequality gred si

description: Mai ElSayed publishes GRED-SI, a geospatial residential-electricity-demand projection model for areas with incomplete electrification. Zenodo archives version 2.0.0 under Apache 2.0 and links the source repository. The release updates how income distributions and growth in electricity access affect demand, with choices to prioritise higher-paying or more disadvantaged population clusters. The repository describes population, income and electricity-access maps as inputs and projected demand layers as outputs for user-defined regions and years. Those layers can feed grid-extension and energy-access planning simulations. No related catalogue record explicitly covers this socioeconomic demand model. A limitation is that income, access and behavioural assumptions drive the projections, and the repository README says some guidance has not yet been updated for the latest release. No archive was downloaded, model run or demand surface checked.
